title: Governance Loss and Allocation Targeting in the Translation of Care Needs in Community Elderly Care Services
content: (1) Background: The conversion of older adults' objective care needs into actual service use remains a challenge in China's community-based care system. This study examined governance loss across demand expression, perceived service availability, and actual use. (2) Methods: Data from 11,648 adults aged 60 years or older in the 2023 China Longitudinal Aging Social Survey (CLASS) were analyzed using a four-stage conversion funnel, cluster-robust logistic regression, concentration indices, and 15 alternative need definitions. (3) Results: Objective care needs affected 42.2% of respondents. Demand expression was 48.3% among those with needs and 40.4% among those without. Only 30.7% of those expressing demand perceived the named service as available, and 19.6% of those perceiving availability used it, yielding an overall conversion rate of 2.9%. Demand expression was associated with functional limitations, multimorbidity, living alone, and urban residence, but not income. Education-related concentration indices were 0.130 for community-based social care and −0.010 for primary medical services. (4) Conclusions: Substantial governance losses occur throughout needs conversion. Proactive needs identification, improved service content, and strengthened access procedures are needed to improve service targeting.
